plan.concept: RANSAC robustly fits models in the presence of heavy noise and outliers by finding the candidate model that gains the highest consensus from the dataset.
learningObjectives: After engaging with this figure, the student will understand how RANSAC uses minimal sample sets (2 points for a line) to generate candidate models.
The student will be able to explain how an inlier threshold distinguishes valid data points from outliers.
The student will be able to describe why the iteration with the maximum consensus represents the optimal robust fit.
plan.keyInsight: Instead of letting outliers ruin a global fit, RANSAC guesses models using random pairs of points; the true model inevitably wins because it gathers a massive 'consensus' of surrounding points.

interactions.label: RANSAC Iteration
interactions.effect: Changes the two randomly selected sample points (red circles), re-draws the resulting fit line, and updates which data points are classified as inliers (blue) versus outliers (white).
interactions.teaches: How different random samples produce wildly different model hypotheses, only one of which will align with the true data structure.

interactions.label: Inlier Threshold
interactions.effect: Visually widens or narrows a shaded tolerance band around the line, dynamically changing which points fall inside (turning them blue) or outside (turning them white).
interactions.teaches: The trade-off of the distance threshold: too narrow and you reject true noisy data; too wide and you include unrelated outliers.

demo_steps.title: A Bad Random Guess
demo_steps.narration: Look at the active red points and the resulting line. In this initial iteration, RANSAC randomly picked one true inlier point and one outlier. Notice how this incorrect model fits the broader dataset poorly, yielding only 2 or 3 inliers because most points lie far outside the shaded threshold band.
demo_steps.focus: The poorly aligned red line and the high number of white outlier points.

demo_steps.title: Adjusting the Tolerance
demo_steps.narration: Keep this poor model but increase the Inlier Threshold slider. Watch how the shaded consensus band expands. While this greedily classifies more points as 'inliers' (blue), it is a false positive—it demonstrates why choosing a precise, physically meaningful threshold is vital to avoid accepting bad models.
demo_steps.focus: The widening shaded band around the line and the artificial conversion of white points to blue.

demo_steps.title: The Consensus Breakthrough
demo_steps.narration: Now, switch to Iteration 3 and reset the threshold to a medium level. RANSAC has randomly selected two points that lie on the true underlying line. Instantly, the consensus skyrockets to 9 inliers (blue circles), while the real outliers (white circles on the right) are successfully ignored. This peak consensus identifies our winning model.
demo_steps.focus: The 9 blue inliers aligned beautifully along the red line, contrasted against the isolated white outliers.

plan.reconstructionNotes: An interactive 2D scatter plot. Displays approximately 12 points: a distinct line of 9 points with slight Gaussian noise, and 3 outlier points clustered far off the line to the bottom right. A red line is drawn based on two highlighted 'active' red points. A semi-transparent shaded envelope (the tolerance band) surrounds the red line, with thickness controlled by the inlierThreshold. Points inside the band are colored light blue (inliers), while points outside are white with black borders. When iteration is 3, the two red points lie on the main line. When iteration is 1 or 2, the red points are chosen poorly (e.g. connecting one line point to an outlier), showing a tilted, incorrect line.
